<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to source for the purpose of running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. This command only evaluates the top-level (global) scope of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, or `package()`. The global variable assignments in this file are standard for AUR packages: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `depends`, `source`, etc., are all declared using simple, static values or predictable expansions (e.g., `$_pkgbase`). The `source` array references a git repository at a specific tag (`v$pkgver`), which is a common and acceptable pattern. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid hash, so no `SKIP` or missing checksum issues arise in this context. There are no command substitutions, dynamic downloads, or data exfiltration attempts in the global scope. All potentially executable logic is confined to functions that are not invoked during `--printsrcinfo`. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD poses no risk of unintended code execution or data leakage.
</details>

Dependencies are appropriate for a GTK4 + libadwaita application and include runtime and build-time requirements.

No evidence of malicious behavior was found. The package follows common AUR packaging practices, including proper use of `source`, `sha256sums`, and standard build lifecycle functions.
